from_notes: GSAT-30 | 17 Jan 2020, Kourou | Telecom
x: GSAT-30, launched from Kourou on 17 Jan 2020, is a telecommunication satellite with C and Ku-band transponders (replacing INSAT-4A).
GSAT-18 (3,404 kg) was launched on Ariane-5 VA-231 from Kourou on 6 Oct 2016 (IST). Resourcesat-2A flew in Dec 2016; GSAT-16 in Dec 2014.
India's communication satellite of October 2016 was GSAT-18 (Ariane-5, Kourou, 6 Oct 2016). GSAT-16 flew in 2014, and GSAT-17 and -19 in June 2017.
Hughes Communications India launched India's first high-throughput satellite (HTS) broadband service in 2022, using capacity on ISRO's GSAT-11 and GSAT-29.

from_notes: GSAT-3 (EDUSAT) 2004 World's first dedicated educational satellite
x: GSAT-3 (EDUSAT, 2004) is India's dedicated educational satellite, linking schools and colleges. INSAT-1B was multipurpose, Aditya-L1 is solar, and Cartosat-1 does mapping.

from_notes: INSAT-3A / 3C / 3E | ... | Broadcasting, mobile, meteorology
x: INSAT-3A (Kourou, 10 Apr 2003) is multipurpose, with broadcasting, communication and meteorological payloads, so it is not only a telecom, TV or weather satellite.

from_notes: GSAT-30 | 17 Jan 2020, Kourou | Telecom; not a Sun-synchronous orbit
x: The false statement is the Sun-synchronous orbit: GSAT-30 is a geostationary telecom satellite placed in a geosynchronous transfer orbit. It went up on Ariane-5 VA-251 from Kourou and serves C and Ku bands.
GSAT-8, a DTH communication satellite with a GAGAN payload, was launched in 2011 on Ariane-5 VA-202 from Kourou, so only option d has the right year; the exact date was 21 May 2011.
dispute: Official key: 21 April 2011. Strictly: GSAT-8 was launched on 21 May 2011 (ISRO GSAT-8 page); no printed date is exact.

from_notes: GSAT-10 | Sep 2012 | Heaviest Indian comsat at that time

from_notes: GSAT-10 | Sep 2012 | Heaviest Indian comsat at that time
x: GSAT-10 (29 Sep 2012) was then India's heaviest communication satellite. OCEANSAT is remote sensing, and LANDSAT and SPOT are US and French satellites.

x: Cyclones are tracked with INSAT meteorological imagers (INSAT-3D/3DR) from geostationary orbit. IRS and Oceansat are low-orbit remote-sensing satellites.
The South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9, May 2017) serves Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (with Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan); Pakistan opted out.
